skill.name: zach-search-term-report-analyzer
skill.description: Analyzes Amazon Ads search term reports for SP, SB, and SD campaigns. It cleans reports, classifies terms, and produces reviewable bid, negative, scale, and listing feedback candidates.
skill.summary: Analyze Amazon Ads search terms and produce reviewable campaign action candidates.
skill.author: zach22-1999

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown inline code, Chinese advertising terminology, Unicode normalization, and readable reference text. Confirmed issues are limited to an actual curl subprocess and Amazon URL fetch path, plus a semantic concern that browser utility comments describe anti-bot evasion behavior.

remediation.issue: Outbound curl subprocess for listing fetches
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl subprocess use with a Python HTTP client, strict ASIN validation, fixed Amazon domains, and clear network timeouts.

remediation.issue: Live listing fetch can run by default
remediation.suggestion: Make network fetching explicitly opt-in and prefer user-provided local listing context for deterministic offline analysis.

remediation.issue: Anti-bot evasion language in scraping utility
remediation.suggestion: Remove wording and behavior intended to bypass detection. Use compliant APIs or user-provided product context instead.

content.value_statement: Amazon Ads search term reports are hard to turn into clear actions. This skill cleans reports, compares time windows, and produces reviewable bid, negative, scale, and listing feedback candidates.
actual_capabilities: Cleans Amazon Ads search term reports from CSV and Excel files.
Maps SP, SB, and SD report fields into standard analysis fields.
Identifies candidate ASINs and separates analysis by one selected ASIN.
Compares 7, 14, and 30 day clicks, spend, orders, CVR, ACOS, and trends.
Classifies terms as brand, competitor, ASIN, category, attribute, scenario, irrelevant, or uncertain.
Generates Markdown, CSV, and run summary outputs for manual review.
limitations: It does not change bids, budgets, negative keywords, or campaign structure.
It needs date, search term, clicks, and spend fields for useful analysis.
Live Amazon listing fetches can fail because of captchas, network limits, or page changes.
Low volume terms and mixed trend signals still need human judgment.

use_cases.title: Review wasted spend
use_cases.description: Find search terms with high spend, weak conversion, or high ACOS before making manual bid or negative keyword decisions.

use_cases.title: Find scale candidates
use_cases.description: Compare recent windows to identify search terms with stronger conversion, better cost efficiency, or improving trend signals.

use_cases.title: Improve listing language
use_cases.description: Extract attribute and scenario terms from real searches, then feed useful phrases into listing and creative review.

prompt_templates.title: Basic report review
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with one report and no live listing fetch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze my Amazon Ads search term report. Choose one ASIN, skip live listing fetch, and summarize the action candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Add listing context
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a local listing context file for relevance checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this search term report with my provided listing context. Highlight attribute, scenario, weak relevance, and listing feedback terms.

prompt_templates.title: Compare trend windows
prompt_templates.prompt: Clean the report, compare 7, 14, and 30 day performance, and separate stable winners from terms needing more data.

prompt_templates.title: Audit action decisions
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a full review with a target ACOS.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the report using a 20 percent target ACOS. Explain the threshold logic and flag every low confidence recommendation for manual review.

output_examples.input: A Sponsored Products search term report for one ASIN with 30 days of clicks, spend, orders, and sales.
output: The report identifies negative keyword candidates, reduce bid candidates, scale candidates, and observe terms.
Each recommendation includes the main reason, confidence, and the time window evidence that supports it.

output_examples.input: A search term report plus a local listing context file for the same ASIN.
output: The analysis marks terms that match product attributes, usage scenarios, or weak listing coverage.
The summary separates campaign actions from listing feedback items for manual follow-up.

output_examples.input: A report containing multiple ASIN candidates.
output_examples.output: The skill stops mixed analysis, lists candidate ASINs, and asks the user to choose one analysis target.

best_practices: Analyze one ASIN at a time so benchmark comparisons stay meaningful.
Use a local listing context file when network access is restricted or repeatability matters.
Treat every bid, budget, and negative keyword action as a manual review candidate.
anti_patterns: Do not mix multiple ASINs and apply one shared CVR baseline.
Do not treat low click volume terms as final winners or losers.
Do not run live listing fetches when the user expects offline-only analysis.

faq.question: What report types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Amazon Ads SP, SB, and SD search term reports exported as CSV or Excel files.

faq.question: Can it change my advertising account?
faq.answer: No. It only produces analysis files and review candidates. Users must apply account changes manually.

faq.question: What fields are required?
faq.answer: The useful minimum is date, search term, clicks, and spend. Conversion fields improve decision quality.

faq.question: Does it need internet access?
faq.answer: No for basic report analysis. Live listing context fetches are optional and can be skipped.

faq.question: How does it handle multiple ASINs?
faq.answer: It identifies candidates and asks for one ASIN. It should not combine unrelated products in one benchmark.

faq.question: What outputs should I expect?
faq.answer: It can produce a Markdown report, CSV detail table, CSV anomaly list, and run summary.
